newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron Jews take over two houses in Arab casbah.
newsitem.headline: Hebron Jews take over two houses in Arab casbah.

text.p: Jewish settlers, angry at progress towards an Israeli government deal with Palestinians to hand over much of Hebron, took over two buildings in the town's Arab casbah early on Wednesday, witnesses said.

They said they broke into the houses only a day after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyanu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat made progress on a long-overdue Israeli handover of much of the West Bank town to Palestinian self-rule.

Israel Radio said about 20 settlers had taken over the buildings and quoted them as saying one was Jewish property and the other a building they feared Palestinians would use to house "terrorists". The radio reported a massive presence of soldiers and police in the town.

Under a 1995 peace deal, Israel is to give Palestinians control of 80 percent of Hebron, holy to both Jews and Moslems as the burial place of the biblical Abraham. The two leaders closed in on a deal during a summit on Tuesday.

The right-wing Netanyahu has conditioned a Hebron agreement on guarantees for the safety of the 400 Jewish settlers in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs which was captured by Israel with the rest of the West Bank in the 1967 Middle East war.
The Arab casbah is in the 20 percent of Hebron due to remain under Israeli occupation in the deal along with the enclaves where the 400 Jews live and study.
